question: What is the primary causative organism of tuberculosis?
explanation: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused specifically by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why must nurses administer multiple anti-TB drugs simultaneously rather than a single agent?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of the hospital stay
options.B: To prevent the rapid emergence of drug resistance
options.C: To shorten the total treatment duration to one week
options.D: To eliminate the need for liver function blood tests

explanation: Single drug therapy allows naturally resistant bacterial mutants to survive and multiply, making combination therapy mandatory. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which first-line anti-TB drug is known to cause orange-red discoloration of body fluids?
explanation: Rifampicin naturally metabolizes into an orange-red pigment that safely tints urine, sweat, and tears. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: A patient taking ethambutol reports blurred vision and trouble seeing green colors. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise the patient to wear sunglasses for outdoor sunlight
options.B: Encourage the patient to increase daily fluid intake
options.C: Tell the patient this is a normal harmless side effect
options.D: Report visual changes immediately as signs of optic neuritis

explanation: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, requiring prompt clinical evaluation and possible drug cessation to prevent permanent damage. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary intracellular target of isoniazid?
explanation: Isoniazid specifically blocks the production of mycolic acids, weakening the unique cell wall of the tubercle bacillus. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h3)

question: How does rifampicin effectively kill tuberculosis bacteria inside the human body?

options.C: By blocking calcium channels in cells
options.D: By dissolving the outer protein capsid

explanation: Rifampicin binds to bacterial RNA polymerase, stopping the transcription process necessary for protein creation and bacterial survival. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the standard total duration for treating drug-susceptible tuberculosis?
explanation: The standard short-course chemotherapy regimen for drug-sensitive TB lasts for a total duration of six months. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: A patient asks why a health worker must watch them swallow their tuberculosis pills every day. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: To guarantee complete adherence and stop drug-resistant strains from developing
options.B: To verify that the patient is eating enough food before taking medications
options.C: To ensure the hospital receives proper funding from international donors
options.D: To measure the exact weight loss occurring during the intensive phase

explanation: Direct observation ensures patients do not miss doses, which is the primary driver of treatment failure and drug resistance. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which major organ system requires close laboratory monitoring during first-line tuberculosis therapy?
explanation: Rifampicin, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide are all metabolized by the liver, making hepatotoxicity a primary risk requiring vigilance. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) routinely prescribed alongside isoniazid?

options.B: To reduce joint swelling and pain

explanation: Isoniazid promotes the excretion of pyridoxine, leading to nerve damage in the extremities unless supplemented. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: Multi-Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is defined as resistance to which two primary medications?
explanation: MDR-TB specifically denotes resistance to the two most powerful first-line anti-TB drugs, isoniazid and rifampicin. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)

question: What makes treating extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) much harder than drug-susceptible cases?

options.A: Second-line drugs are more toxic and require much longer treatment times
options.B: Patients with XDR-TB do not experience any physical symptoms of illness
options.C: Infection rates drop significantly because the bacteria cannot reproduce
options.D: Standard sputum tests cannot detect the presence of XDR-TB strains

explanation: XDR-TB regimens involve alternative medications that are harsher on the body and must be taken for nearly two years. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)

question: A patient on month three of TB treatment stops taking medications because their cough has stopped. What should the nurse explain?

options.A: Stopping medication prevents further liver damage from occurring
options.B: Stopping early allows surviving bacteria to multiply and cause drug-resistant disease
options.C: The patient can switch to herbal remedies for the remaining months
options.D: The remaining pills are only required if family members start coughing

explanation: Feeling better does not mean the infection is cleared; stopping treatment prematurely causes relapse and drug resistance. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which infection control practice should nurses teach newly diagnosed active pulmonary TB patients?

options.A: Boiling all drinking water for at least twenty minutes
options.B: Isolating family members in separate buildings permanently
options.C: Covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gloves during daily household chores

explanation: TB spreads via airborne droplets, making proper cough etiquette and ventilation essential infection control practices. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h7)
